title: Systemic Biological Mechanisms of Neurocognitive Dysfunction in Long-term Survivors of Childhood Hodgkin Lymphoma
notes: Cross-sectional analysis of childhood HL survivors (mean 20.5yr post-diagnosis, mean age 35.4) vs age/sex-matched community controls. Comprehensive neuropsych battery (12 domains) + inflammatory biomarkers (IL-6, TNF-α, hs-CRP, OxLDL, GPx, MDA, homocysteine, etc). Biomarker tertile analysis + elastic net multi-biomarker models. IL-6 specifically associated with visuomotor processing speed; CRP broadly associated with 7 cognitive domains; MDA and homocysteine each associated with 2-3 domains. Mediation: CRP mediated vascular→sustained attention (39.6%), visual processing speed (70.9%); IL-6 mediated pulmonary→visuomotor processing speed (36.8%). 45% survivors had CRP≥3 vs 28% controls. Higher chest radiation (>30Gy) → higher CRP (β=0.65) and homocysteine (β=0.23). No CNS-directed therapy in sample.
null_findings: IL-6 tertile effects NOT significant in community controls
CRP associations NOT identified in controls
TNF-α: only 2nd tertile associated with long-term recall (not 3rd), may be spurious
OxLDL: not significantly associated with any cognitive outcome
IL-10, IL-8: not measured in this study
